questions.question: ______ are gently sloping areas of the ocean basins
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Deep sea plains**__.

__
 
• **Deep-sea plains are gently sloping areas of the ocean basins**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Ocean Floor Division can be divided into various parts such as Continental Shelf, Continental Slope, Continental Rise or Foot, Deep Ocean basins, Abyssal plains or Deep Sea plain, Oceanic Trenches, Seamounts, and Guyots.
 
 
• **Deep-Sea Plain or Abyssal plain**

 
 
• These plains are gently sloping areas of the ocean basins.
 
• These are the flattest and smoothest regions of the world.
 
• It is an underwater plain on the deep ocean floor, usually found at depths between 3,000 and 6,000m.
 
• These plains are covered with fine-grained sediments like clay and silt.
 
• Lying generally between the foot of a continental rise and a mid-ocean ridge, abyssal plains cover more than 50% of the Earth’s surface.
 
 
 
• **Oceanic Deeps or Trenches**
 
 
• These areas are the deepest parts of the oceans.
 
• The trenches are relatively steep-sided, narrow basins.
 
• They are some 3-5 km deeper than the surrounding ocean floor.
 
• They occur at the bases of continental slopes and along island arcs and are associated with active volcanoes and strong earthquakes.
 
 
 
• **Continental Shelf**
 
 
• The continental shelf is the extended margin of each continent occupied by relatively shallow seas and gulfs.
 
• It is the shallowest part of the ocean showing an average gradient of 1° or even less.
 
• The shelf typically ends at a very steep slope, called the shelf break.
 
 
 
• **Continental Slope**
 
 
• The continental slope connects the continental shelf and the ocean basins.
 
• It begins where the bottom of the continental shelf sharply drops off into a steep slope.
 
• The gradient of the slope region varies between 2-5°.
 
• The depth of the slope region varies between 200 and 3,000 m.
 
• The slope boundary indicates the end of the continents.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT one of the reasons why the public sector played a dominant role in establishing the Industrial sector in India post-independence?

options.text: Poor savings capacity of the public
To avoid generation of private profit
Absence of large enough market for output
Lack of adequate capital with private industrialists

questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** To avoid generation of private profit.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **Poor savings capacity of the public:**

 
 
• This was one of the main reasons why the public sector played a** **dominant role in establishing the industrial sector in India post-independence.
 
• The private sector did not have enough capital to invest in large-scale industries, and the government had to step in to fill this gap.
 
 
 
• **Absence of a large enough market for output:**
 
 
• Another reason why the public sector played a dominant role was that there was not a large enough market for the output of the industries.
 
• The private sector would have found it difficult to sustain their businesses in such a scenario, and the government had to step in to provide the necessary infrastructure and support.
 
 
 
• **Lack of adequate capital with private industrialists:**
 
 
• As mentioned earlier, the private sector did not have adequate capital to invest in large-scale industries.
 
• The government had to provide the necessary capital through various means such as subsidies, tax incentives, and loans.
 
 
 
• **To avoid the generation of private profit:**
 
 
• This option is incorrect because it goes against the basic principles of capitalism and entrepreneurship.
 
• The private sector is driven by the profit motive, and this is what encourages innovation, efficiency, and growth.
 
• The government's role is to facilitate this process by creating a conducive environment for businesses to thrive.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Industrial sector in India post-Independence:**

 
 
• The Indian government adopted a socialist approach to economic development after Independence in 1947.
 
• The focus was on building a self-sufficient economy through import substitution and state-led industrialization.
 
 
 
• **Private sector in India: **
 
 
• **​**The private sector was largely absent in the early years of Independence, as the government had nationalized many key industries.
 
• It was only in the 1980s and 1990s that the government started liberalizing the economy and allowing private participation in various sectors.
 
 
 
• **Public sector in India: **
 
 
• **​**The public sector played a dominant role in the Indian economy for several decades after Independence.
 
• The government set up various public sector enterprises in key industries such as steel, coal, power, and telecommunications.
 
• These enterprises were supposed to be the engines of growth and development for the country.

questions.question: In the context of mapping climate data, what term refers to a line drawn through all points on a map that contain the same amount of cloud?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Isoneph:-**

 
 
• **It refers to a line drawn through all points on a map that contain the same amount of cloud. **
 
• It is a type of isoline, which is a line that connects points of equal value.
 
• **Other common isolines include contour lines (elevation), isobars (atmospheric pressure), and isotherms (temperature).**
 
• Isonephs are used by meteorologists and climatologists to visualize the distribution of cloud cover over a region.
 
• **They can be used to identify areas of high and low cloud cover, as well as to track the movement of clouds over time.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Isohels:-**

 
 
• These are lines drawn on a map that connect points of equal sunshine duration.
 
 
 
• **Isocheims:-**
 
 
• These are lines drawn on a map that connect points of equal temperature.
 
 
 
• **Isochalaz:-**
 
 
• These are lines drawn on a map that connect points of equal hail size.

questions.question: In which color are the railway lines and telephone lines shown in the topographic map ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Black**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **railway lines** and **telephone lines** shown in the topographic map are in **black color**.
 
• **B****lack ****Color in the topographic map**: All riverbanks, broken grounds, dry streams, surveyed trees, heights and their numbering, railway tracks, telephone and telegraph lines.

questions.question: Which continent provides more than half of world's tin?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Asia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Asia continent produces more than half of the world's tin.
 
• In Asia, China is the major producer of tin.
 
• Tin is found in the ore cassiterite.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Asia is the largest continent & It covers about one-third of the total land area of the earth.
 
• The continent lies in the Eastern Hemisphere. The Tropic of Cancer(23 1/2° N) passes through this continent.
 
• Asia is separated from Europe by the Ural mountains on the west.
 
• The combined landmass of Europe and Asia is called Eurasia (Europe + Asia).
